entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 30
1Sa 30:1-5 . The Amalekites Spoil Ziklag.
1. Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag-- While the strength of the Philistine forces was poured out of their country into the plain of Esdraelon, the Amalekite marauders seized the opportunity of the defenseless state of Philistia to invade the southern territory. Of course, David's town suffered from the ravages of these nomad plunderers, in revenge for his recent raid upon their territory.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2807"/><div sID="gen3850" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2807"/><hi type="bold">2. they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away--</hi>Their conduct seems to stand in favorable contrast to that of David (<reference osisRef="1Sam.27.11">1Sa 27:11</reference>). But their apparent clemency did not arise from humane considerations. It is traceable to the ancient war usages of the East, where the men of war, on the capture of a city, were unsparingly put to death, but there were no warriors in Ziklag at the time. The women and boys were reserved for slaves, and the old people were spared out of respect to age. <div eID="gen3850" type="x-p"/>

David was greatly distressed--</hi>He had reason, not only on his own personal account (<reference osisRef="1Sam.30.5">1Sa 30:5</reference>), but on account of the vehement outcry and insurrectionary threats against him for having left the place so defenseless that the families of his men fell an unresisting prey to the enemy. entries.content_plain:
6. David was greatly distressed-- He had reason, not only on his own personal account ( 1Sa 30:5 ), but on account of the vehement outcry and insurrectionary threats against him for having left the place so defenseless that the families of his men fell an unresisting prey to the enemy. Under the pressure of so unexpected and widespread a calamity, of which he was upbraided as the indirect occasion, the spirit of any other leader guided by ordinary motives would have sunk;
but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God-- His faith supplied him with inward resources of comfort and energy, and through the seasonable inquiries he made by Urim, he inspired confidence by ordering an immediate pursuit of the plunderers.
entries.reader_content_plain:

Under the pressure of so unexpected and widespread a calamity, of which he was upbraided as the indirect occasion, the spirit of any other leader guided by ordinary motives would have sunk;
but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God-- His faith supplied him with inward resources of comfort and energy, and through the seasonable inquiries he made by Urim, he inspired confidence by ordering an immediate pursuit of the plunderers.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2814"/><div sID="gen3860" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2814"/><hi type="bold">16. they were spread abroad upon all the earth--</hi>Believing that David and all his men of war were far away, engaged with the Philistine expedition, they deemed themselves perfectly secure and abandoned themselves to all manner of barbaric revelry. The promise made in answer to the devout inquiries of David (<reference osisRef="1Sam.30.8">1Sa 30:8</reference>) was fulfilled. The marauders were surprised and panic-stricken. A great slaughter ensued--the people as well as the booty taken from Ziklag was recovered, besides a great amount of spoil which they had collected in a wide, freebooting excursion. <div eID="gen3860" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv2816"/><div sID="gen3862" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv2816"/><hi type="bold">26. when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil to the elders of Judah--</hi>This was intended as an acknowledgment to the leading men in those towns and villages of Judah which had ministered to his necessities in the course of his various wanderings. It was the dictate of an amiable and grateful heart; and the effect of this well-timed liberality was to bring a large accession of numbers to his camp (<reference osisRef="1Chr.12.22">1Ch 12:22</reference>).
